what: This repository's own judge, audited on answers that are wrong by construction.
why: Every accuracy number this project publishes is the judge's opinion, and the campaign resolves two or three questions on a 121-question capability. The published LoCoMo audit reports that a standard judge accepted 62.81% of topical-but-wrong answers; this repository had never measured its own.

artifact.why: the artifact the campaign is currently read from, not the previous one

workflow: judge-audit.yml dispatched with run_id=41159983913, limit=120, model=deepseek-chat (GitHub run 41173396348)
criterion: false-accept Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%. NOT MET at 26.2%.

predictions.name: a wholly wrong gold is caught
the rate is larger than the effect

registrationNote: 13.182.3 registered the plan counts as 167 (59/51/57) because it was computed on run 40989420944; the dispatch audited 41159983913 and planned 160 (61/49/50). The refusal of a case is per-question, so the count moves with the artifact. The predictions are about rates and are unaffected; the count is recorded here rather than corrected in the registration.
limits: One judge (deepseek-chat with the official templates), one perturbation family. It does not measure agreement with a human, and it does not transfer to answers that are wrong by omission — a plausible half-answer, which is the shape the MR failures were already found to have.
The perturbations substitute tokens; an answer that is wrong because it omits something is not audited here.
Absention questions are excluded: their template asks whether the model recognised the question as unanswerable, so substituting a name does not make the answer wrong.
120 questions yield 160 cases, not the 419 accepted answers in the artifact; a larger limit would tighten the bound, not move the direction.
